pr_title: HTTP/3: Improve static table compression to include values
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33980

Improves on https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/38565

When writing known headers, check if the value also matches a static table entry. If it matches then write just an index for name and value.

issue_context.title: Implement Http3 static response header compression
issue_context.body:
Http3 (QPack) supports a static list of headers that can be used for compression. This is implemented today for decoding request headers but not when encoding response headers.

We support the same feature for Http/2 here:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b9efadc59ddbf6743775244622fb95301dd1846c/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2HeaderEnumerator.cs#L145-L150

review_comments: @pranavkm Array initialize indenting was messed up when file scoped namespaces were introduced.

Yup. I noticed it too. There's also some nesting for lambdas that are messed up. I'll get a PR to clean it up.

FYI @davidwengier in case you wanted to have a look at it (or perhaps this is resolved as part of your trivia fix).

Sadly, its a long standing limitation of the formatter, that it doesn't touch collection, object and array initializers. Unfortunately when file scoped namespaces come along and de-indent everything, that fact becomes very visible. The issue is tracked in https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/8269
